Data sources
  • Geography: county boundaries from US Census data (us-atlas), distances to 57 metro anchors, computed here.
  • Fiber: distance to the nearest colocation or network facility, from the CAIDA IXP dataset (built on PeeringDB), Oct 2026 release. Facility locations only, not fiber routes.
  • Carbon reference: the US grid averages about 384 kg CO₂e per MWh (Ember 2025). There is no industry standard cap, so the caps here are examples. Tenants usually set clean energy goals instead.
  • Policy: state actions found in public sources in Nov 2026. Moratorium tracker, ArentFox Schiff, Venable, NCSL. Verify before relying on any state.
  • Energy: the hourly model covers ERCOT only, from the case packet. Outside Texas the Overall grade uses the regional grid queue wait as a stand in, until hourly prices for those regions are added.
  • Water: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water stress, matched to counties here.
  • Time to power: LBNL Queued Up (data through 2025), by grid operator area.
  • Wind and solar cap: EIA Hourly Electric Grid Monitor, 2025 net generation by grid operator (via Catalyst Cooperative's PUDL).
  • Hazard: FEMA National Risk Index v1.20 (Dec 2025), expected building loss per dollar of buildings.

1Reliability · how far the plan can be pushed

Plan rules
Why we cap wind and solar

A plan that gets 80% or 90% of its energy from wind and solar looks cheap on paper, but real systems do not run that way without very large storage or firm backup. For scale, EIA hourly data for 2025 shows ERCOT, SPP and CAISO each got 37% of their energy from wind and solar. Among the 31 US grid operators above 15 TWh, the highest was Colorado's Xcel area at 45%, and the only one above that was a small New Mexico utility (PNM, 71%), which leans on its neighbors. Plans above the cap are removed before anything is ranked, and a plan within the cap still has to ride through a 5 day drought and the site's own grid stress case without leaving load unserved. The stress case can be made harsher but not softer than the site's own.

Alerts and actions

Data and model. Power costs, carbon, demand and its tiers, wind and solar profiles, prices, grid schedule, stress events and the seven resource offers come from the contestant packet; builds start from 384 pre-simulated plans that passed its official checker and are re-run hour by hour in your browser with the checker's accounting. Revenue models, demand growth, weather years, contract delays, forecast events and the rented generator ($350/MWh, 0.74 t CO₂/MWh) are ours and labeled. The packet does not allow selling power back to the grid. Cost is the packet's decision cost (energy, equipment, contracts, $123.50/MWh to move work, $1,000/MWh for paused batch work), constant 2023 dollars, undiscounted. Dispatch follows simple rules, not an optimizer.
